messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — GPU queue growth detected in us-west-2 pool (pool-id: gw-prod-gpu). Current queued requests: 12.5k, 90th p90 latency spike, autoscaler attempts 4/5 failed. Paging oncall.

oncall-alex: I'm on it. can someone paste the autoscaler error logs? @sre-jamie please join. :phone:

sre-jamie: looking. initial glance: autoscaler tried to add nodes but API rate-limited by cloud provider and then driver OOMs started showing on newly-created nodes. sequence looks like: scale attempt -> node up -> driver crash -> node flaps -> backlog increases.

eng-runtime-maya: confirming — runtime metrics show KV cache warmup skyrocketing mem usage on first few model shards. saw repeated CUDA/Xid 79 and 4 in dmesg. stack traces attached below. will post short logs.

eng-runtime-maya: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:08:00): 79, PID=21234 GPU a0
Runtime: model_shard_07 OOM on allocate kv_cache 256MB -> trace ...
autoscaler: scale-up attempt id=eu-3402 retry=2 -> error: "RateLimitExceeded"
node-init: driver start -> crash -> systemd restart -> repeated
```

infra-lee: cloud quota for GPUs in us-west-2 is at 98% due to another customer's long-running Dedicated pool. We can't scale past the account cap right now. I've opened a support ticket but won't get quota raised immediately.

product-kai: customers on Standard tier may see elevated latencies — what do we think the blast radius is? any specific customers impacted? @customer-success-ana

customer-success-ana: I have two active accounts reporting slow responses from their inference endpoints — both use large embeddings and batch pipelines. I flagged them and started messages. They asked for ETA.

oncall-alex: triage plan:
1) throttle non-critical routes and reduce max tokens on background batches
2) set fallback routing to smaller quantized model variant where possible
3) prevent autoscaler from repeatedly spinning nodes (we'll pause it) and instead warm a small pool by provisioning pre-baked images
4) engage runtime to patch driver OOM mitigation

sre-jamie: executing 1 & 3 now. throttling rule applied to route: /v1/embeddings.batch (weight=0.25). autoscaler set to paused via feature-flag: AUTOSCALE_PAUSE=true for gw-prod-gpu pools.

oncall-alex: timeline notes and commands:
- throttles: `curl -X POST https://console.internal/throttle -d '{"route":"/v1/embeddings.batch","factor":0.25}'`
- pause autoscaler: `kubectl patch cm autoscaler-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"paused":"true"}}'`

eng-runtime-maya: patched the runtime to avoid aggressive KV preallocation for new nodes. small hotfix rolling now (will skip large cache growth on cold-start). patch id: rt-hotfix/2026-03-15-1

eng-runtime-maya: hotfix log:
```
apply patch rt-hotfix/2026-03-15-1
skip-kv-prealloc=true
restart runtime pods gw-prod-gpu-shard-* sequentially
```

infra-lee: because we can't scale GPUs beyond quotas, I'm provisioning a small burst of CPU fallback backends (gpu-fallback-cpu-1..4) and routing lower-priority models there. this should reduce queue pressure for non-latency-critical work.

product-kai: good. can we prioritize customer-facing low-latency routes on the remaining healthy GPUs? otherwise we risk SLO misses for paid customers.

sre-jamie: applied per-route priorities. pinned high-priority routes to existing healthy nodes (node-23, node-29). Verified token-per-second rates dropped for the throttled routes; backlog decreased from 12.5k -> 6.2k in 8 minutes.

customer-success-ana: update: one customer acknowledged and is ok with temporary throttling if we provide ETA. asking for note to send: short summary + expected mitigation steps.

oncall-alex: creating quick customer note: "We are experiencing GPU capacity pressure in us-west-2 due to autoscaler retries + driver instability. We've applied throttles, enabled CPU fallbacks for batch jobs, and rolled a runtime hotfix. Estimated recovery window ~30-60m. We'll follow up with RCA." @customer-success-ana please send.

customer-success-ana: sent to impacted accounts. they appreciate the transparency.

eng-runtime-maya: runtime logs after hotfix are looking better. no new Xid 79s on restarted pods for 3 consecutive restarts. memory growth is within expected delta. continuing to monitor.

infra-lee: cloud support updated ticket: temporary quota bump request pending, ETA unknown. we can possibly shift some Dedicated capacity to this account but that will require org-approval. I've DM'ed ops lead.

sre-jamie: autoscaler remained paused; I'm scheduling a controlled manual scale: will add 2 nodes with the hotfix image and CGroup memory limits adjusted to prevent driver-side OOM. command:
```
cloudctl compute create --image hotfix-rt-2026-03-15 --gpus 2 --label gw-prod-gpu-temp
```

oncall-alex: please watch for node flapping after those come up. if any node shows repeated driver restarts, we'll cordon and drain then reimage.

sre-jamie: new nodes up, one node reported transient driver panic then stabilized. cordoned node-412 -> drained -> reimage started.

eng-runtime-maya: observed a subtle race during model shard load causing transient allocations — fix queued for post-incident, but the hotfix mitigates the fatal path.

sre-jamie: backlog now 1.1k. 90th latency trending down to 420ms from 1.6s peak.

product-kai: I want to note feature flag workflow that caused autoscaler to retry aggressively — we had exponential backoff disabled for this pool. that's probably why we hit cloud rate limits faster. will file follow-up.

oncall-alex: agreed. immediate next steps:
- keep autoscaler paused for 30m, monitor backlog and latency (sre)
- confirm runtime patch holds after 3h (runtime)
- prepare customer postmortem draft (ops + product)

eng-runtime-maya: will follow metrics. I'll also capture heap dumps from one of the earlier crashed pods for deeper analysis.

customer-success-ana: some customers asked for a timeline for a follow-up summary. i'll coordinate language with product-kai.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED — severity: P2 -> P3 (mitigated). notes: autoscaler paused, runtime hotfix applied, CPU fallback in effect.

oncall-alex: thanks all. handing off to SRE for watch window. i'm repping in #oncall-handoff in 15m.

sre-jamie: taking watch. ping me if backlog rises > 2k or Xid errors resume.

eng-runtime-maya: filing follow-ups: RT-2462 (root cause triage), RT-2463 (hotfix hardening), RT-2464 (kv-cache safe-init). will link relevant crash dumps.

product-kai: I'll draft customer-facing postmortem and coordinate with legal for any contractual notices.

customer-success-ana: will update impacted customers with post-incident note once draft ready.

oncall-alex: closing the live-thread. thanks team :heart:
_meta_note: This thread simulates a Slack incident coordination chat. Messages are in chronological order and include system bot messages, on-call coordination, mitigations, commands, logs, and customer comms. All fields are strings or list of strings as required.
